text: Williamson's knowledge-first program defends the knowledge norm of assertion. Which statement gives the norm together with its main supporting consideration?
choices: Assert P only if P is true; supported by the claim that asserting a falsehood is always criticizable regardless of the speaker's epistemic position.
Assert P only if you justifiably believe P; supported by cases in which a reasonable but false assertion still seems beyond reproach.
Assert P only if you know P; supported by the aptness of the challenge 'How do you know?' and the infelicity of Moorean assertions such as 'P, but I don't know that P.'
Assert P only if you believe P; supported by the sincerity condition that an assertion expresses the speaker's own belief.
explanation: For Williamson, assertion is constitutively governed by knowledge: a speaker who asserts P without knowing it is criticizable ('I didn't know it, I was guessing'), and Moore-paradoxical assertions are infelicitous because asserting P represents oneself as knowing P. The truth norm (0), justified-belief norm (1), and belief norm (3) are the principal rivals that Williamson argues are either too weak or face counterexamples the knowledge norm handles naturally.
